// why: The reference input of the negative control: a minimal but CORRECT picture of the workspace, in which every TypeScript file is seen by some compiler. Every case beside it is built on a copy of this one and brings in exactly one defect, so a case file holds the defect alone rather than one more copy of a correct input. Were this reference itself defective, every case would fire because of it — which is why the gate checks it separately.
// projects: Three projects cover three different situations at once: a library with TWO disjoint programs (the package and the specs), a project with not one TypeScript file (tokens — deliberately with no target, because demanding one would demand the checking of an empty set) and the root project, whose root `.` is a prefix of everything and which collects only what nobody else took.
// seen: The compiler program, that is what `tsc --listFilesOnly` prints in a real run. The key is the project name, not the command: a project is sometimes several programs at once and only their UNION is meant to cover its files.
